key_insight: A multimodal cardiac foundation model pretrained on data from 1.7 million individuals can interpret heart signals and associated text across both hospital and at‑home devices, delivering consistent, device‑agnostic cardiac insights.
problem_solved: Bridges device and setting variability (hospital ECGs vs. wearable/home monitors) and limited labeled data by learning a shared representation from massive, multimodal cardiac datasets.
method: Pretrain a multimodal foundation model on raw heart signals (ECG/PPG) paired with textual interpretations from 1.7 million individuals to learn joint signal–text representations.
Use representation learning to align data from diverse devices and settings, enabling robust transfer and inference across hospital and at‑home recordings.
Fine‑tune or prompt the pretrained model for downstream cardiac tasks (diagnosis, triage, summary generation) across heterogeneous devices.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a scalable, device‑agnostic backbone for cardiac applications that reduces domain shift and annotation needs, accelerating deployment of interoperable cardiac analytics across clinical and consumer settings.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: large multimodal pretraining dataset (1.7M individuals) → foundation model → downstream cardiac tasks
Device strip: icons for hospital ECG, smartwatch/patch, and home monitor with arrows showing unified model handling each input
Performance/robustness chart: metric comparisons across device types and settings (hospital vs home) showing stable performance
Embedding visualization: t-SNE/UMAP demonstrating aligned signal–text representations across devices
paper_title: Cardiac health assessment across scenarios and devices using a multimodal foundation model pretrained on data from 1.7 million individuals
paper_authors: Xiao Gu, Wei Tang, Jinpei Han, Veer Sangha, Fenglin Liu
